newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan stocks end at record on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan stocks end at record on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks hit a record high Wednesday, buoyed by continued strong foreign bids for Venezuelan blue chips, traders said.
The bolsa's 19-share index closed up a solid 0.46 percent at 6,894.82 points, according to preliminary figures from the exchange. The last record set was 6,878 on January 3.
"Foreigners are snapping up blue chips," said Financorp broker Miguel Ortiz. Despite six consecutive rises, "Prices are still good and I believe the trend is still up."
Steel company Sivensa led the gainers, rising 5.36 percent to end at 177.00 bolivars.

Venezuelan stocks have languished since their last January high, sadly lagging the region's other roaring bourses. But the today's record close puts the market on new ground, New York-based analysts IDEA said in a market comment.
"We look for a new high next week ... (and) a target of 6,947 points," IDEA said.
Trade volume reached nearly 45 million shares, worth 5.3 billion bolivars ($10.9 million), as 21 stocks rose, 14 fell and six closed flat.
Activalores broker Gustavo Alonso said Sivensa had been helped by the apparent progress through Congress of steel company Sidor's privatization contract.
Sivensa is one of the pre-selected bidders in Sidor's auction, slated for July.
Foreign interest had been further piqued "by the oil opening, which is basically a done deal, and should bring a river of dollars into the country in the second half of the year," Alonso added.
Venezuela is due to auction operating contracts to 20 oil fields next week in its third oil opening round.
Despite the day's net rise, the market opened off as investors did some long-expected profit-taking.
But "the adjustment was not as large as everyone had previously thought," said Ortiz.
Merinvest's composite index .MRCP meanwhile rose 0.63 percent to end at 109.58 points.
